messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] feature request for log(x-y); given log(x) and log(y), i.e. a log_diff_exp(xl, yl)
parts:
I added it to the to-do list. I'd been meaning to
do something like this before. To match log_sum_exp,
I'd want to call it something like this:

log_diff_exp(x,y) =def= log(exp(x) - exp(y))

and then we can use the same rescaling track to avoid
overflow on the exp.

I'm not convinced the snippet you linked implements this
the most efficiently and arithmetically stable way possible.
Cutting out boundaries and renaming, here's that code:

// copyright Andrew Miller, downloaded from http://snipplr.com/view/12707/
double
log_diff_exp(double x, double y) {
double diff = x - y;
diff /= 2.0;
return (x + y) / 2.0 + log(exp(diff) - exp(-diff));
}

Given that we know x > y, we can just do this:

log(exp(x) - exp(y))

= log(exp(x) * (exp(x)/exp(x) - exp(y)/exp(x)))

= log(exp(x)) + log(1 - exp(y)/exp(x))

= x + log(1 - exp(y - x))

= x + log1m(exp(y-x))

Because x > y, 0 <= exp(y-x) <= 1.

Is that the right thing to do here or is it better to use
the above form from the snippet linked above?

- Bob
